subject: Private GPU pool: deployment density targets, egress mitigation, and ops manifest
messages:
From: Tim Sullivan <tim.sullivan@vertexcloud.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 17 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private GPU pool - initial ask: density & egress constraints

Mina / team,

Thanks for taking this call earlier. As discussed, VertexCloud is finalizing network segmentation and rack population plans for a colocated private deployment. Before we lock in racks we need a short written capacity target and a list of network mitigations so our facilities team can validate cross-connect egress and firewall policies.

Key asks from our side:
- Expected sustained throughput (tokens/sec) per 8x A100-equivalent rack under mixed chat + embedding workload.
- Deployment density (how many inference pods per GPU, typical concurrency envelope).
- Egress profile: peak concurrent outbound flows per minute (to fetch KV caches / model artifacts / metrics).
- Any required L4/L7 firewall rules or keepalive thresholds we should record for the operations runbook.

Can you send a concise plan (1-2 pages) we can attach to our procurement docs by EOD Monday (Oct 19)? If helpful we can schedule a 30m engineering review Tue/Wed.

Thanks,
Tim
Tim Sullivan
Cloud Ops Lead, VertexCloud
ops@vertexcloud.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool - initial ask: density & egress constraints

Tim — thanks for the clear list. I've sketched a short manifest below and attached a simple density model + egress calc for your ops team to review. High level summary first (details in attachment):

Summary (for procurement):
- Sustained throughput: plan for 180k–240k tokens/sec per 8x A100-equivalent rack under a 70/30 chat/embedding mix with Redwood serving runtime and kv-prefix caching enabled. This range reflects conservative and optimized kernel paths (70k–90k tokens/sec per GPU effective).
- Deployment density: default is 1 inference pod per GPU (1:1) for strict latency SLOs. For cost-density tradeoffs we support 1.5–2x multiplexing (up to 2 client virtual pods per GPU) when 95th latency SLO can relax by ~25–40ms depending on prompt length.
- Concurrency envelope: expect sustained concurrency of ~6–10 streams per GPU for chat workloads; bursts up to ~20 streams with admission control and warm-pool capacity.
- Egress profile: plan 60–150 outbound flows/min per rack for model artifact refreshes, metrics, and KV warmups under typical traffic. Allow for spiky bursts up to ~400 flows/min during deploy windows.
- Network requirements: 25 Gbps top-of-rack uplink recommended per 8x GPU rack for mixed workloads; prefer private peering for telemetry and artifact fetches. L4: allow ports 443 and 22000 (runtime control plane) to Redwood control plane IPs. Keepalive: TCP keepalive 60s; idle flow timeouts >= 120s to avoid premature KV eviction.

I attached: density_model_v1.xlsx (density math and examples), egress_mitigation_calc.csv (flow estimates), private-deploy-manifest-v0.3.md (short ops manifest).

Next steps: if that range looks good we should run the warm-pool sizing exercise on Monday (I can spin a quick sim with our traffic mix). Happy to meet Tue 10:00 PT with engineering.

Cheers,
Mina Haddad
Sr. PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

Attachments: density_model_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), egress_mitigation_calc.csv (csv), private-deploy-manifest-v0.3.md (markdown)

Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool - initial ask: density & egress constraints

Quick technical notes from infra: 

- Kernel path variance: the 70k–90k tokens/sec per GPU is realistic for medium-length prompts (<= 512 tokens) with optimized attention kernels. For longer sequences expect linear degradation; we recommend explicit per-VM CPU pinning for NVMe-accelerated KV caches to keep tail latency stable.
- Admission control: implement a two-tier admission (fast-path for pinned low-latency routes, slow-path for multiplexed tenants) — this prevents noisy neighbors from pushing a rack to the 400 flows/min burst envelope.
- Egress mitigation: suggest an egress proxy that performs artifact caching and a burst throttle at the ToR to convert spikes into a controlled ramp. We have a reference config in the attachment: private-deploy-manifest-v0.3.md section 4.
- Observability: expose token-level cost and per-request KV-hit metrics out of the runtime; recommend pushing a 1s-aggregated telemetry stream to your private collector to avoid telemetry storms on public endpoints.

I'll join Tue 10:00 PT for the sim review.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

1) Our colo network team wants the exact ToR burst throttle value to program into their policer (they asked for a recommended pps value).
2) They asked for a one-line statement we can include in the contract about acceptable telemetry egress (what telemetry rate you will guarantee to keep from hitting our uplink).

If you can push a one-paragraph addendum to the manifest with those two numbers we can attach to the contract by EOD. Otherwise we'll need to schedule a 30m call with procurement later this week.

Tim

Tim — adding the requested contract-friendly addendum below; Mina/Jonas, please confirm and I'll paste into the manifest PDF.

Contract addendum (proposed):
"Redwood Inference will dimension telemetry exports to VertexCloud's private collector at a sustained maximum of 1200 events/sec aggregated per 8x GPU rack (1s aggregation). During controlled deployment windows (pulls, cache warmups) short bursts of up to 5000 events/sec for up to 120 seconds may occur; Redwood will coordinate deployment windows with VertexCloud and will use Top-of-Rack (ToR) burst shaping to smooth egress. Recommended ToR policing: 8k packets/sec sustained with a 30k packets burst allowance (100ms token-bucket burst window) to accommodate short-lived artifact refreshes."

Action items:
- Mina: incorporate the addendum into private-deploy-manifest-v0.4.md and drop the PDF into the Drive link (due Wed 10:00 PT).
- Jonas: include ToR proxy config snippet and pps example in the manifest (due Wed 10:00 PT).
- Vanessa: coordinate with Customer Success on a training call for VertexCloud ops (propose Thu 11:00 PT).

Tim — once Mina drops the updated manifest we'll route it to procurement.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
